sections.h2: Where does Montcalm County keep its land records?
sections.html:
Every Montcalm County deed lands in one place, the register of deeds in Stanton at 211 W. Main St. (box 368, Stanton, MI 48888). Treasury's statewide directory lists 989-831-7337 and regofdeeds@co.montcalm.mi.us. Phone ahead for counter hours and for the electronic filing rules, since staff set both.

Voters moved the county seat from Greenville, the seat since 1840, to Stanton in 1860. Stanton is tiny, 1,348 residents in 2020, and it occupies the point where Day, Evergreen, Sidney and Douglass townships touch. A parcel in any township of the county, from Carson City to Vestaburg, is recorded here.

sections.h2: What do Greenville and Stanton tell a seller about the market?
sections.html:
Greenville is the largest city, with 8,816 residents in 2020. It lies 16 road miles southwest of Stanton and about 33 miles northeast of Grand Rapids, which explains why Montcalm is counted in the Grand Rapids metropolitan area. The Flat River runs through town, and Baldwin, Manoka and Como lakes sit inside the city limits. Greenville built its name on refrigerator manufacturing, and it was the birthplace of the Meijer store chain. The Electrolux plant closed in 2006, a loss that affected 2,700 employees and their families.

Around the city, farms grow potatoes, corn and Christmas trees and run dairy herds. The Fred Meijer Heartland Trail ends in Greenville after 41 miles from Alma, and the Flat River Trail loops the city. A house near a lake or trail often draws a buyer who wants the recreation, so mention those features in your listing.

The city's roots go back to 1844, when a settler built a sawmill on the Flat River, and Danish immigrants followed. Ranney Refrigerator Company opened in 1892 and earned Greenville the label Refrigerator Capital of the World. Hendrik Meijer opened his first grocery there in 1934. Stanton, by comparison, is a government town whose ZIP code, 48888, is shared with parts of Ferris, Belvidere and Pine townships.

  • Greenville's Lafayette Street downtown district was placed on the National and State Register of Historic Places in 2008.
  • The Danish Festival fills the third weekend of August.
  • The Montcalm County 4-H Fair is held in Greenville each summer.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Montcalm County?
sections.html:
Rural living dominates: 84.6% of residents are outside urban areas, spread across 705 square miles of land. The 2020 count of 66,614 grew to an estimated 69,406 by July 2025, and 20.1% are 65 or older.

Owners live in 83.1% of occupied housing. Half of owner-occupied homes were worth under $185,500 in 2020 to 2024 figures, rent at the median ran $869 and median household income reached $67,344. A one-way trip to work averages 30.7 minutes, and the Census tally for 2025 shows 201 building permits.

Families choose among eight public districts: Carson City Crystal Area, Central Montcalm, Greenville, Lakeview, Montabella, Tri County Area and Vestaburg, with the Montcalm Area ISD coordinating services. Montcalm Community College anchors higher education.

sections.h2: What will the recording fee be in Montcalm County?
sections.html:
Section 2567 of the Revised Judicature Act prices recording at a flat $30.00 a document. If one paper assigns or discharges multiple instruments, each beyond the first costs another $3.00. Copying runs a dollar a page, and a certificate on a recorded paper is $5.00.

Money is due with the paper. An electronic filing gets one extra business day. Charter counties alone may set other amounts, so confirm the Stanton figures before mailing a check.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax would a Montcalm County seller pay?
sections.html:
On a Montcalm sale, the grantor carries both taxes, due at the county treasurer in the 15 days after the deed is handed over. The state portion is $3.75 and the county portion $0.55 per $500 or part of $500. The table prices a sale at the county's median home value.

Family handovers get special treatment. The state act excludes a deed from a parent to a child or grandchild, and it excludes foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu. The county act has no family exclusion, so the county share can still apply. Whichever exemption fits, write it on the deed itself.

sections.h2: Which formatting rules can get a deed bounced in Stanton?
sections.html:
The register works from MCL 565.201 and may refuse a paper that misses a requirement, which costs you a trip. Walk through this list with your closing agent.

  • Signatures in black or dark blue ink, each with the printed name below it that the notary also used.
  • Grantee addresses and the drafter's name and address written on the deed.
  • A top margin of 2.5 inches on the first page, half an inch elsewhere.
  • A first line identifying the one event being recorded.
  • Ten-point print on white 20-pound paper between letter and legal size.
  • Social Security numbers cut to their last four digits.

A translation must be attached to any foreign-language paper. Staff cannot advise on or write the document.

sections.h2: How does a sale change the tax bill and the homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Taxable value normally climbs at the lesser of 5% or inflation each year. A sale breaks that cap: the next year's taxable value resets to state equalized value, which is half of true cash value. Residential transfers to a parent, child, sibling or grandchild who will not use the home commercially are excepted, which can help an heir.

The new owner must tell the assessor within 45 days. Meanwhile the register sends the assessing offices a monthly list of recorded transactions.

In Michigan, tax assessment belongs to cities and townships, not the county, so your local assessor handles exemptions and affidavits even though the deed goes to Stanton.

If you took the principal residence exemption, send Form 2602 to your township or city assessor within 90 days of leaving. Lateness costs $5 per day up to $200, and the exemption ends on December 31. A buyer who will live in the house files Form 2368 by June 1 or November 1.

sections.h2: Can I sell an inherited or rundown Montcalm County house?
sections.html:
Yes. An heir needs authority to sign, usually through the estate's personal representative, and a certified death certificate may need to go on record if a deed names a surviving owner. The deed from the estate follows the same recording steps as any other.

A cash buyer who takes the property as it stands skips lender appraisals and repair demands, though transfer tax, recording and the assessor notice still apply. Ask the county treasurer for the parcel's tax status first, since a delinquent balance should be settled before you set a closing date.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed for a house near Greenville?
faqs.a: Stanton's register of deeds, even for a Greenville address, because Montcalm County has a single recording office at 211 W. Main St. Treasury's directory lists 989-831-7337.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies at a $185,500 price?
faqs.a: $1,595.30 in total: $1,391.25 to the state and $204.05 to the county, paid by the seller. Prices round up in $500 steps before the rates apply.

faqs.q: Will the register review my deed form?
faqs.a: Staff check that a paper meets recording standards and then record it. Drafting is outside their role, so bring a finished deed prepared by an attorney or title company.

faqs.q: Do the buyer's taxes go up after a sale?
faqs.a: Typically yes, since ownership change moves taxable value to the state equalized value the next year. The buyer notifies the assessor within 45 days, and some family transfers keep the old value.

faqs.q: How soon must I drop my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Within 90 days of moving out, on Form 2602 filed with the local assessor. After that, $5 per day accrues until it reaches $200.
